Google just claimed the top spot on the Artificial Analysis benchmark with Gemini 4 Carbon, passing Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra.

Today brought a series of notable updates across enterprise AI, frontier model benchmarks, and workplace automation.

Here are the key takeaways from today's releases:

🚀 Google launched Gemini 4 Carbon, taking the top spot on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index (v5.0) benchmark ahead of Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra. Google highlighted improvements in coding, agentic tasks, and cybersecurity.

👁️ Public access to Carbon is currently unavailable. Early coverage points out that Gemini 4 Carbon functions essentially as a slightly improved version of Google's Argon model.

💼 OpenAI and ServiceNow expanded their partnership. The integration brings OpenAI models and AI agents into ServiceNow, while introducing ServiceNow workflows directly into ChatGPT and Codex.

🎓 Google added a student hub to the Gemini app. The update rolls out immersive explorations designed for users learning new topics inside the application.

As a developer, seeing Gemini 4 Carbon lead the Artificial Analysis benchmark over GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5.5 shows how fast frontier performance is shifting. Meanwhile, connecting ServiceNow workflows into Codex and ChatGPT highlights how AI agents are moving directly into day-to-day developer and enterprise tools.

Are you more focused on benchmark gains or deep enterprise integrations right now?
